newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish bonds ease amid Buba talk, markka rebounds.
newsitem.headline: Finnish bonds ease amid Buba talk, markka rebounds.

text.p: Bonds were lower and money rates higher in relatively active trade as Bunds weakened on German rate jitters, but the long end was supported by a shift from shorter instruments, dealers said.

"Investors were selling at the short end and buying at the long end," one money market dealer said. The dealer said investors were shifting out of fear that if the Bundesbank raised rates, the Bank of Finland may follow.
The markka fell on profit-taking from recent gains in line with other Scandinavian currencies, despite mark weakness.
"The markka weakened as foreign investment banks sold it for marks on the thin New York market late on Thursday, and this continued here, too, in the morning," one forex dealer said.
"Bundesbank's vice president Gaddum's comment today that earlier agreed ERM parities were still suitable, triggered a market reaction towards 3.04 (in DEM/FIM)," he said.
Gaddum also said the dollar was overvalued. Traders said this was verbal intervention, and many expected it to be followed by Bundesbank dollar sales.
"If that comes (and does not work), then I will expect a German rate hike," a dealer said.
